rule: Every value below was returned by a function in reference/mochimo-wots or by the bs58 it calls, and every input was read from group_c_addr.json. Nothing here is transcribed and nothing is hand-computed. Regenerate rather than edit.

oracle.why: Two implementations of one algorithm, and they can disagree. The C in reference/mochimo-core computed the `crc16` and `base58` columns of crc16_base58_corpus in group_c_addr.json by calling crc16() and base58_encode(); the TypeScript in reference/mochimo-wots -- addrTagToBase58, composing its own crc() with the bs58 package -- computed the values here from the same thousand tags, and neither derives from the other. This is errata 37 independence in its strong form: the second implementation was EXECUTED, not read. What it adds over group CX is not a subject but a sample. CX crosschecks this encoder on the four `tag` vectors group C’s `vectors` array holds -- C7 all-zero, C8 all-ff, C9 the tag whose expected string the upstream test file states, C10 all-zero plus a bit, with C7 and C9 also carrying transcribed upstream literals -- and all four are boundaries somebody predicted, so they are evidence about the failures that were predicted and silent about the rest. Four points also cannot distinguish a CRC whose polynomial is right from one whose initial value compensates on those four. The thousand tags here were chosen by sha256 and by nobody; what they actually span is recorded in corpus_census, recomputed each run, rather than argued in this sentence. The corpus was already on disk and was a C-against-itself record until this program ran over it.
oracle.domain: Every entry of group_c_addr.json’s `crc16_base58_corpus.entries` -- a thousand tags, each the first 20 bytes of sha256(ull_to_bytes(i, 8)) as the block’s own note records. The domain is read out of the artifact rather than listed here, the entry count is compared against the block’s independently written `count`, and each entry’s `i` is compared against its position, so a corpus that grew, shrank or was reordered stops the run instead of producing a file whose `crosschecks_vector` names the wrong subject. The block sits beside group C’s `vectors` array rather than in it, which is why group_c_crosscheck.ts -- whose domain is that array -- never reached it.
oracle.not_an_oracle: The CRC16 recovered here is NOT a direct call to the second implementation’s crc() and must not be counted as one. crc() is not exported from the mochimo-wots package, so the value is read back out of addrTagToBase58’s own output: it cannot separate a wrong CRC from a compensating bug in the encoder, because both live inside one function. Neither is group C’s own `crc16` column a second opinion about its `base58` column -- the C generator produced both, so they cannot disagree with each other. And C7 and C9, the two tags in this subject carrying transcribed upstream literals, are deliberately crosschecked in group_c_crosscheck.json and not here; a literal copied into this file would be a second transcription of one reading, not a second reading. corpus_census is not an oracle either: it is arithmetic over the values above, so it can show what the sample spans and can never show that the span was enough.

corpus_census.note: Recomputed from the corpus on every run. It is arithmetic over the values emitted above, not a protocol claim, and it exists so the oracle block’s argument -- that a thousand uncurated tags reach further than four chosen boundaries -- is a figure a reader can check rather than a sentence to believe.
